reels.title: Nuclear drills every week: why we constantly wait for the apocalypse
reels.hook: Every week they waited for the atomic bomb
reels.why: A personal story with a clear picture (school drills facing the Soviet bomb) transitions into a universal insight about fear of the future. It ends optimistically and well-rounded.
reels.speaker: Damir Omerbegović
reels.quote: I think it is in human nature to constantly think in some kind of apocalyptic scenarios in one's head.

cards.text: Every week they waited for the atomic bomb
Damir Omerbegović, socio-political commentator
Damir's American friend recalls childhood in American schools.
Childhood in the Cold War
I think it is in human nature to constantly think in some kind of apocalyptic scenarios in one's head.

reels.title: Bosniaks, Sharia and “milk sheikhs”
reels.hook: Do Bosniaks know what a Sharia state is?
reels.why: A provocative claim already in the first sentence, and the humorous label “milk sheikhs” gives it a memorable point. It is short and understandable without context.
reels.speaker: Damir Omerbegović
reels.quote: Bosniaks are a very secularized people.

cards.text: Do Bosniaks know what a Sharia state is?
Damir Omerbegović, commentator born in Tuzla
Answer to the question whether Bosniaks are ready for a Sharia state.
Bosniaks are a very secularized people.
Partly as a joke, I call them milk sheikhs.
DAMIR OMERBEGOVIĆ – On BiH after the elections, on political Islamism – PODCAST ČUŠPAJZ #169

reels.title: Why Bosniaks look toward Iran, Maduro, and Putin
reels.hook: Iran, Maduro, Putin – why them in particular?
reels.why: The guest rejects the popular thesis about foreign powers and offers a clear explanation. The closing sentence is strong and easily quotable.
reels.speaker: Damir Omerbegović
reels.quote: The key problem with Bosniaks is that they try to find themselves in a world they do not understand, and by God, neither does the world understand them very well.

cards.text: Iran, Maduro, Putin – why them in particular?
Damir Omerbegović, socio-political commentator
A conversation about foreign influences on Bosniak society.
“Alternative” to right-wingers and Dodik
They try to find themselves in a world they do not understand, and by God, neither does the world understand them very well.

reels.title: Riots in Paris, peace in Prague: what is the difference?
reels.hook: Paris is burning, Prague is not. Why?
reels.why: Starts with a sharp, controversial claim and substantiates it with personal experience from Prague. Ends with a clear conclusion about the approach to migration.
reels.speaker: Damir Omerbegović
reels.quote: Evidently multiculturalism itself is not the problem.

cards.text: Paris is burning, Prague is not. Why?
Damir Omerbegović, commentator, lives in Prague
Question: are the riots in France a consequence of a lack of apartments and jobs?
That long Damir has lived in Prague
Foreigners he lives and works with
Evidently multiculturalism itself is not the problem.

reels.title: Is Dayton to blame for all of BiH's problems?
reels.hook: Is Dayton to blame for everything?
reels.why: A short and well-rounded insight with a very quotable sentence about compromise as treason and blockade as victory. Understandable to anyone from the region.
reels.speaker: Damir Omerbegović
reels.quote: Compromise often presents itself as some kind of treason, and institutional blockade as some kind of patriotic victory.

cards.text: Is Dayton to blame for everything?
Damir Omerbegović, socio-political commentator
The Dayton Agreement stopped the war and created today's constitution of BiH.
Compromise is often presented as some kind of treason, and institutional blockade as some kind of patriotic victory.

reels.title: Islamic Declaration: is one allowed to criticize Alija Izetbegović?
reels.hook: Is one allowed to criticize Alija Izetbegović?
reels.why: A sensitive topic covered with measure: the role in the struggle for independence is acknowledged, but a critical reading is called for. A strong concluding sentence.
reels.speaker: Damir Omerbegović
reels.quote: In a healthy society that should not be anything disputed, but there it is, among Bosniaks it still is.

cards.text: Is one allowed to criticize Alija Izetbegović?
Damir Omerbegović, writes about Bosniak identity
The subject is Alija Izetbegović's Islamic Declaration from 1970.
That text is key to understanding how this situation in which we find ourselves today came to be.
In a healthy society that should not be anything disputed, but there it is, among Bosniaks it still is.

reels.title: America has flying cars, the EU deals with bottle caps
reels.hook: America builds flying cars, the EU regulates bottle caps
reels.why: A familiar internet meme gets an unexpected twist: dealing with a bottle cap is a sign of peace. It is humorous, and the point is clear.
reels.speaker: Damir Omerbegović
reels.quote: And it is a very good thing that we are dealing with a bottle cap.

cards.text: America builds flying cars, the EU regulates bottle caps
Damir Omerbegović, socio-political commentator
Answer to the question whether Brussels bureaucracy leads to total control.
Meme: flying car vs. bottle cap
I would rather deal with a bottle cap than be thinking about how we will make weapons.

reels.title: Why the students succeeded where the opposition did not
reels.hook: Why did the students succeed where the opposition did not?
reels.why: A clear analysis of a hot topic: students united people around simple questions of accountability. It has a beginning, development, and conclusion.
reels.speaker: Damir Omerbegović
reels.quote: And when such a social energy is created, then it can obviously become a serious political force.

cards.text: Why did the students succeed where the opposition did not?
Damir Omerbegović, socio-political commentator
In the elections in Serbia, the student list defeated Vučić.
It all began with a tragedy
When such a social energy is created, then it can obviously become a serious political force.
